episode_title: Chiropractors Solving Chiropractic Problems: 5 Lessons From Our First 3,000 EHR Users

real_qa.q: What is the 30-second documentation goal for interim visits in ChiroUp EHR and how does it work without sacrificing note quality?
real_qa.r: ChiroUp set a goal of 30 seconds for an interim visit note and one minute for a new patient note. The key is that the doctor is not responsible for creating every element of the note—staff and patients contribute information through digital intake forms and automated functional assessment questionnaires. The doctor clarifies details rather than typing everything, allowing faster documentation without compromising accuracy and detail.
real_qa.requete: ChiroUp 30 seconds interim visit documentation goal

real_qa.q: How does ChiroUp's dynamic patient intake survey differ from static template-based surveys in chiropractic EHR systems?
real_qa.r: ChiroUp's survey changes the next question based on the patient's previous answer, acting like a virtual intern that collects relevant information dynamically. Unlike static surveys with 9,000 templates, the dynamic system asks only pertinent questions—if a patient reports low back pain, it automatically collects the Oswestry; if they mention an auto accident, it triggers auto accident questionnaires. This ensures each survey adapts to the patient's specific condition rather than forcing them through irrelevant questions.
real_qa.requete: ChiroUp dynamic intake survey vs static templates

real_qa.q: What are the limitations of generic AI scribe transcription for chiropractic documentation according to ChiroUp's experience?
real_qa.r: Generic AI scribes that transcribe entire visit conversations create inaccurate and messy notes because they cannot distinguish clinical details from extraneous conversation—they cannot identify which vertebral segments the doctor is treating, what orthopedic tests were performed, or what actually happened in previous visits. Full transcription often requires more cleanup time than creating the note manually, and the systems make significant errors on objective findings and assessment sections critical to chiropractic records.
real_qa.requete: AI scribe limitations chiropractic documentation objective findings

real_qa.q: How does ChiroUp's ChiroPvote crowdsourcing system influence software feature development?
real_qa.r: ChiroPvote allows subscribers to submit feature ideas directly into the system, where other users can upvote and suggest improvements. Rather than developers guessing what chiropractors need, coding bandwidth is allocated based on subscriber demand—for example, when subscribers requested membership and package features, that became the next released feature. This approach means crucial features come from subscribers in the trenches rather than from company assumptions.

real_qa.q: Why did ChiroUp take six months to design the chief complaint survey and what did that reveal about chiropractor preferences?
real_qa.r: It took six months to design, implement, code, test, and roll out the chief complaint survey. However, the rollout revealed that every chiropractor wanted something different—different questions, different layouts, different field types. This discovery led to the fundamental lesson that you cannot build a great chiropractic EHR for chiropractors; you can only build it with chiropractors because every practitioner operates differently.
real_qa.requete: ChiroUp chief complaint survey six months design lesson
